programmes.name: Sutton Trust UK Summer Schools
programmes.summary: A free summer school of about a week at a leading university: undergraduate-level teaching in one subject, UCAS and personal statement help, and a lower offer from some host universities.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students in England or Wales who attend, and have always attended, a state-funded, non-fee-paying school or college. The Sutton Trust looks for students who would be the first in their family to go to university, have had free school meals, attend a school with below-average results or low progression to university, live in a low-progression or deprived neighbourhood, or have been in care. Five GCSEs at grades 9-6 including English and Maths are desirable.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Must always have attended a state-funded, non-fee-paying school/college and be in Year 12 in England or Wales (Year 13 in Northern Ireland, S5 in Scotland); generally you need to be under 18. Desirable: at least five GCSEs at grades 9-6 (A*-B) including English and Maths; universities may look at overall GCSE results and some courses have subject requirements. You don't need to meet every extra criterion, but the more you meet the more likely you are to get a place. Care-experienced applicants only need the age, school and academic requirements. You can apply for one course only and can't already be on another Sutton Trust programme, so it can't be combined with Pathways. 2026 course requirements: Durham Economics and Finance needs A-level Maths; Durham Accounting needs A-level Maths or GCSE Maths grade 6 or above; Durham Business needs GCSE Maths grade 6 or above (or Core Maths grade B); Imperial needs three A-levels including Maths and eight GCSEs with at least five at grades 7-9; Nottingham needs GCSE Maths grade 6; Southampton Economics needs GCSE English and Maths at grade 4 (Business: Maths grade 6, grade 5 accepted); Warwick PPE needs GCSE Maths grade 7; St Andrews needs a GCSE or National 5 in English and Maths; Sheffield and Glasgow have no extra subject requirements.
benefits: Completely free; travel costs are covered
Over 15 hours of undergraduate-level teaching in your chosen subject
UCAS, personal statement and student finance workshops
Access to Sutton Trust Online and the Sutton Trust alumni network
A lower offer from some host universities (Durham, Nottingham, Sheffield, St Andrews, Southampton, Glasgow)
programmes.offerReduction: Depends on the host university (Sutton Trust table, 2026). Durham: a guaranteed contextual offer, typically at least two grades below the standard offer (if you attend Durham's summer school). Nottingham: two grades off (one grade off if you attended another university's summer school); needs Home fee status and a most recent school that wasn't independent. Sheffield: up to three grades off, down to BBC (up to two grades off if you attended elsewhere and meet its Access+ criteria). St Andrews: you become eligible for its minimum entry requirements. Southampton: a lower offer for participants of its Experience UoS residential who meet its criteria. Glasgow: an adjusted offer if you meet its widening participation criteria (UK applicants from outside Scotland are usually offered the minimum grade requirement). Imperial and Warwick give no extra consideration for the summer school, and Edinburgh doesn't guarantee a contextual offer.
programmes.subjects: All subjects (40+ subject areas). Economics, business, finance and social science courses in 2026: Economics and Finance, Accounting and Business (Durham); Economics, Finance and Data Science (Imperial); Business, Maths and Economics (Nottingham); Management and Economics (Sheffield); Economics and Business (Southampton); Economics and Management (St Andrews); PPE (Warwick); Arts & Social Sciences (Glasgow)

programmes.name: Pathways to Banking & Finance Online (Sutton Trust)
programmes.summary: A free online programme over Year 12 and 13 with banking and finance employer and university taster sessions, skills workshops, online work experience, mentoring and application support, open to students anywhere in the UK.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students in England or Wales (Year 13 in Northern Ireland, S5 in Scotland) anywhere in the UK who have always attended a state-funded, non-fee-paying school or college. Selection also looks at five GCSEs at grades 9-6 including English and Maths, being first in the family to go to university, free school meals, a school with below-average results or low progression to university, a low-progression or deprived neighbourhood, and time in care.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: No commuting needed: the online programmes are open to anyone across the country (the in-person Pathways need you to live within 90 minutes of the host university). The application is a short form, mostly yes/no questions, plus a personal statement of no more than 300 words. Most sessions are recorded so you can watch later. You can only be on one Sutton Trust programme, so taking a Pathways place rules out a UK Summer School. The in-person Pathways to Banking & Finance programmes at LSE, Leicester, Liverpool and Warwick are listed under those universities.
benefits: Employer- and university-led taster sessions, skills workshops and work placements with leading banking and finance employers (Year 12)
